title: AKL Multi-Model Copilot, Autonomous Agents & Token ROI
description:
Join us for an exclusive evening with visiting GitHub Engineers **Marco Celon** and **Amanda Tan** as we explore the next evolution of AI-assisted software development. Beyond traditional code completion, modern developer workflows now demand seamless orchestration across multiple surfaces, diverse AI models, and autonomous agents—all while keeping enterprise token budgets under control.

Whether you are looking to supercharge your personal developer flow or scale AI productivity across an entire organization, this session delivers actionable strategies straight from the team building these tools.
What We'll Cover:

* **Multi-Surface & Multi-Model Integration:** Learn how to route developer workflows across IDEs, CLI tools, and cloud agents while leveraging diverse models (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini) tailored to task complexity.
* **Token ROI & Cost Control:** Master practical techniques for context window optimization, prompt hygiene, and enterprise budget caps to keep token consumption efficient and cost-effective.

**Agenda**
5:30 - Pizza and networking
6:00 - Talks
7:00 - Finish

title: The Singularity: Are We There Yet?
description:
This session is about the singularity – whether we're in it, approaching it, or talking about something that was never going to arrive the way we imagined.

If you've only encountered the term in headlines, you'll leave with a clear sense of where the idea came from, what its original proponents actually claimed, and why serious people disagree about it.

If you've been following the arguments for years, we'll get into the harder ground: what a threshold would look like from the inside, why every proposed test has failed so far, and what the current evidence genuinely supports versus what gets read into it.

We'll work through three questions in particular – whether a singularity is happening, how we could possibly tell, and what follows if it is. Each demands different tools. The first is empirical and messy. The second is a measurement problem that may not have a solution. The third is where the disagreements get sharpest, because it's where values enter and the evidence runs out.

This is a group discussion, not a lecture. Papers and data will be presented for the room to react to – claims from both directions, including ones that undercut the position most people walk in holding.

No prior background is assumed, and nothing will be treated as too obvious to explain.

We'll explore-

* What "singularity" was originally meant to mean – Good's intelligence explosion, Vinge's horizon of prediction, Kurzweil's curves, and how the term drifted from a specific mechanism into a mood.
* Recursive self-improvement – the load-bearing assumption in most singularity arguments, whether current systems do it at all, and what would count as the real thing.
* The detection problem – if a threshold were crossed, what observation would tell us? We'll look at proposed criteria and where each of them breaks.
* Continuity versus discontinuity – whether progress is exponential, sigmoid, or a series of plateaus, and what the historical record of technological transitions actually shows

title: When I Saw You (Jordan 2012) 1.30 mins
description:
We are in a season of films on Sunday afternoon about films about life in a war zone, especially Palestine.
I have chosen films that are not propaganda.
The attempt is to lift ourselves above that and do a deep dive into the realities of lie in such areas. In this film, Tarek and his mother, Ghaydaa, cross the border from Palestine to Jordan along with tens of thousands of other people.

**When I Saw You** was selected at as the Palestinian entry for the best foreign language film at the Academy Awards. The New York Times reviewer wrote:
"A soft-centered child's-eye view of alienation, toughened by fine acting and Hlne Louvart's full-bodied photography."

The Total Film reviewer wrote: "political without point-scoring, Jacir remains true to a child's-eye view, with Asfa's delightful, exuberant performance always upfront."

"Palestinian filmmaker Annemarie Jacir's second film is slight yet significant - and, because of the situation in Syria, timely - story about a boy whose courage inspires hope among the hopeless."

A must-see for us all as we a look into the lives of familes fleeing from war - anywhere.
